SMT. SUPRIYA SULE (BARAMATI): 

Budgetary Announcements

1. A total outlay of ₹2,78,030 crore has been allocated to the Ministry of Railways in the Union Budget 2026-27. This represents a 10.8 per cent increase over the revised estimate of ₹2,50,920 crore for FY 2025-26. Furthermore, the total capital expenditure for the railways is projected at ₹2,93,030 crore.

2. In a major push for security, a sum of ₹1,20,000 crore has been earmarked for safety-related measures. These include track maintenance, locomotive and coach upgrades, and the rapid installation of Kavach, India?s indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system, along with overhead electrical infrastructure.

3. Additionally, the Finance Minister announced seven new high-speed rail corridors in her budget speech. These corridors, intended to connect five South Indian states among others, will be developed at an estimated total cost of ₹16 lakh crore.

4. Despite these investments, the sector continues to face several persistent challenges. They are:

a. Capital expenditure grew faster than earnings or other operational metrics

(i) Railways? capital expenditure grew at an average annual rate of 17 per cent between 2017-18 and 2023-24, increasing from Rs 1,01,985 crore to Rs 2,62,217 crore.

(ii) However, the total revenue grew at a much slower rate of 6.2 per cent, from Rs 1,78,929 crore in 2017-18 to Rs 2,56,093 crore.

(iii) The capital output ratio (COR), which measures capital employed per unit of traffic (in NTKM for freight and passenger traffic), rose at an annual average rate of 7.7 per cent, from 418 paise in 2017-18 to 704 paise in 2023-24. When adjusted for inflation, the data reveal no improvement in the efficient use of capital.

(iv) Additionally, despite a higher capital outlay, there has been no noticeable improvement in train speeds.

b. Increase in Lease Liabilities

(i) The Indian Rail Finance Corporation (IRFC) borrows from the market and employs a leasing model to finance the acquisition of rolling stock (locomotives, coaches, wagons) and infrastructure projects.

(ii) In 2017-18, these liabilities were Rs 1.6 lakh crore. However, under the 2026-27 Budget, these leasing arrangements are estimated to be Rs 4.3 lakh crore.

(iii) Lease charges consist of both interest and principal components, both of which have seen a steady increase over the last few years.

(iv) Interest expenditure is projected to grow from approximately ₹9,000 crore in 2017-18 to ₹35,130 crore in 2026-27. Simultaneously, principal repayments are estimated to rise from ₹7,980 crore to ₹39,650 crore over the same period.

(v) Consequently, total lease obligations in 2026-27 are expected to consume 25 per cent of internal revenue, a sharp increase from the 19 per cent recorded in the previous year.

c. Delays

(i) According to a 2024 flash report, 848 of the 1,820 monitored projects were facing significant delays, with an average time overrun of 36.59 months. Consequently, the anticipated completion cost for these projects had surged by more than 18.5 per cent over their original estimates.

(ii) The Hindu also observed that project agencies were frequently failing to report revised cost estimates and commissioning schedules, which suggests that current figures for time and cost overruns may be underreported, and the actual final impact could be substantially higher.

(iii) The Flash Report identifies 16 primary causes for these delays, which included challenges in land acquisition, forest and environmental clearances, inadequate infrastructure linkages, financing hurdles, law and order issues, and geological surprises.

(iv) To address these bottlenecks, the Standing Committee (2026) has recommended the establishment of a structured mechanism focused on improved project planning, the parallel processing of approvals, and the prioritization of high-impact connectivity projects.

(v) It further advocates for a targeted and scientific approach to evaluating new railway line proposals. The Committee suggests that proposals must be given due weightage based on traffic projections, the bridging of missing links, and the augmentation of saturated corridors to ensure operational efficiency.

d. The Bullet Train Project

(i) The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project was sanctioned in December 2015 with an initial budget of ₹97,636 crore.

(ii) However, the project has encountered significant time and cost overruns attributed to delays in land acquisition, statutory clearances, and the finalization of rolling stock specifications.

(iii) As of November 30, 2025, overall physical progress stood at 55.6%, while financial progress reached 69.6 per cent.

(iv) The Standing Committee (2026) noted that the cost escalation is primarily driven by additional taxes and cess (₹29,330 crore), rolling stock and signaling requirements (₹16,500 crore), inflationary pressures (₹19,084 crore), and higher costs for land acquisition and resettlement (₹16,695 crore).

(v) Consequently, the Committee has recommended the Ministry to adopt a robust execution framework to enhance inter-agency coordination and expedite utility shifting.

(vi) Furthermore, the Committee has suggested Railways undertake a comprehensive study of successful international high-speed rail networks to integrate global best practices in planning, execution and operations.

e. Quality of Service

(i) Punctuality index measures the share of passenger trains arriving on time at their destination, based on an allowed delay of up to 15 minutes from the scheduled time.

(ii) In 2024-25, Railways recorded a punctuality index of 77 per cent.

(iii) However, CAG (2021) noted that several other countries follow stricter standards, with allowable delays of a few seconds in Japan, three minutes in the Netherlands, five minutes in Germany and Russia, and 10 minutes in the UK.

(iv) An audit analysis of about 13 lakh train runs during 2016-17 and 2018-19 found that only 30 per cent of trains arrived on time, while 20 per cent arrived early, and the remaining 50 per cent were delayed. However, CAG (2021) noted that early arrivals could also be due to schedule padding, reflecting inefficiencies in timetabling.

(v) It also noted that Railways does not specify delivery timelines or fixed schedules for the majority of freight trains, making it difficult to operate goods trains on a timetable. This has an adverse impact on freight speeds and operational efficiency.

(vi) CAG (2025) also found shortcomings in the enforcement of contract conditions at Clean Train Stations (CTS), a scheme for the mechanised cleaning of bio-toilets, doorways, etc, during the 10-15 minutes halt of trains at enroute stations. However, joint inspections at 29 CTS revealed limited cleaning and shortfalls in the use of machines and deployment of manpower.

(vii) Quick Watering Facilities (QWFs) are mechanised supply systems designed to fill multiple train coaches simultaneously during short station halts. However, these facilities were non-operational at 25 per cent of the 109 stations designated for this purpose. This infrastructure gap led to over one lakh complaints in 2022-23 regarding the lack of water in train toilets and washbasins.

(viii) CAG (2025) also observed that passenger feedback on the quality of linen was not effectively enforced on contractors.

f. Safety

(i) While the Railways has taken significant steps to enhance safety, consequential accidents, serious incidents such as collisions, derailments, or fires resulting in casualties, property loss, or major traffic disruptions, remain a concern.

(ii) Between 2000-01 and 2024-25, a total of 3,984 consequential train accidents occurred, including 40 in 2023-24 and 31 in 2024-25.

(iii) A 2021 CAG report identified the primary causes of derailments as: improper driving or speeding, inadequate track maintenance, track parameter deviations exceeding permissible limits, mechanical defects in coaches or wagons, and operational errors during shunting.

(iv) Furthermore, the CAG highlighted a shortfall ranging from 30% to 100% in track condition inspections and observed that 63% of assessed non-AC coaches lacked fire extinguishers.

g. Low private participation

(i) The Indian Railways remains a publicly owned and operated system, with private participation primarily restricted to Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models and outsourcing arrangements.

(ii) According to the Ministry of Railways (2024), private involvement in line projects remains limited, as significant construction risks reduce their attractiveness to private investors.

(iii) Consequently, the Standing Committee on Railways (2025) recommended a more ambitious approach to infrastructure creation, suggesting higher PPP targets to decrease reliance on budgetary support.

(iv) However, Extra Budgetary Resources (EBR) from PPPs are estimated at only ₹12,000 crore for 2026-27, a significant decline from ₹22,116 crore in 2017-18 and ₹24,281 crore in 2018-19.

(v) Structural constraints, particularly in large-scale projects like Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs), continue to hinder investment.

(vi) DFCs require high capital requirements, long gestation periods, and revenue uncertainty stemming from the Ministry?s traffic allocation decisions.

(vii) The Committee on Restructuring of Railways (2015), had noted that this stagnation was largely due to the Ministry of Railways simultaneously holding the roles of policy formulator, regulator, and operator. Hence, these functions must be separated to foster private growth.

h. Increase in Operating Ratio

(i) The Standing Committee on Railways has observed a substantial increase in revenue expenditure over the years, rising from ₹1,38,236 crore in 2020-21 to a projected ₹2,99,500 crore in 2026-27.

(ii) This trend has persisted over the past decade with revenue expenditure absorbing nearly all internal earnings and averaging close to 99 per cent of total receipts.

(iii) Consequently, the generation of a revenue surplus remains limited, severely constraining the Railways? ability to fund capital works from its own internal resources.

(iv) The Operating Ratio (OR) measures the amount spent to earn every ₹100. It serves as a key indicator of financial health and a higher ratio reflects poorer performance.

(v) The Operating Ratio for Railways has deteriorated from 94.6% in 2010-11 to a targeted 98.4 per cent in 2026-27.

(vi) Furthermore, the 2025-26 estimate of 98.8 per cent exceeded the initial budget projection of 98.4 per cent.

(vii) This near-100 per cent operating ratio has led to the chronic underprovisioning of essential funds, including the Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF) for asset renewal, the Capital Fund for debt servicing, and the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) for the upgradation of critical safety assets.

i. Human Resource Management

(i) Loco pilots within the Indian Railways are increasingly seeking safeguards against unsafe infrastructure, excessive administrative pressure, and a stressful work environment.

(ii) Long working hours continue to impact their health and family life, while the non-fulfillment of enhanced kilometer allowances remains a key grievance.

(iii) According to the All India Loco Running Staff Association, pilots are frequently compelled to work beyond the prescribed duty norm of 'nine plus one' hours, significantly increasing stress levels and taking a toll on their physical and mental well-being.

(iv) Furthermore, several locomotives still lack basic washroom facilities, causing severe inconvenience, particularly for women drivers during long-haul journeys.

(v) Media reports indicate that over 30,000 posts of loco running staff remain vacant, personnel are often recalled for duty after barely 14 hours of rest, despite rules prescribing 16 hours of rest plus two hours of preparation time.

(vi) In response to the Railway Recruitment Board?s 2026 notification to fill 22,000 posts, the General Secretary of the All India Railwaymen's Federation (AIRF), expressed serious concern in a letter to the Railway Minister. He stated that the notified vacancies are substantially lower than the actual requirements projected by Zonal General Managers.

(vii) This discrepancy, particularly in workshop vacancies, results in a distorted figure that overlooks the vital role workshops play in safety-critical maintenance.

(viii) Thus, a realistic and transparent vacancy notification process is essential to strengthen operational efficiency and reinforce confidence among both aspiring candidates and current employees.

(ix) On February 17, 2026, media reports revealed that a group of over 70 loco pilots (mail) under the Mumbai Division of Central Railway had jointly applied for voluntary retirement.

(x) The pilots alleged that persistent systemic issues had rendered their working conditions physically exhausting, mentally stressful, and professionally unsustainable.

(xi) Their primary grievances included substandard and unhygienic food, poorly maintained running rooms, excessive administrative pressure, and unsafe infrastructure and restricted access.

j. Freight Traffic

(i) According to Niti Aayog?s Strategy for New India @ 75 (2018), despite Indian Railways? extensive reach and substantial growth in freight volumes, its modal share of surface freight has declined sharply from 86.2 per cent in 1950?51 to just 33 per cent in 2015.

(ii) A critical bottleneck is that routes that constitute only 15 per cent of the total rail network carry 52 per cent of all passenger traffic and 58 per cent of the total freight load.

(iii) This concentration highlights the severe saturation and over-utilization of capacity on the network?s most vital corridors.

(iv) The report then goes on to acknowledge that because passenger and freight traffic share the same tracks, Railways has struggled to achieve significant improvements in speed or capacity relative to global benchmarks.

(v) NITI Aayog (2023) noted that freight charges were almost three times the passenger charges as of 2018-19.

(vi) In 2025-26, freight revenue is estimated to be 5.1 per cent lower than budgeted and revenue from passenger services is expected to fall short by 13.8 per cent compared to the budget target.

k. State of fencing

(i) Railway line fencing is essential for the safety of citizens and the Railway administration has administered this work. However, farmers have been complaining that the said work is encroaching upon their private lands and the railway authority does not possess official documentary evidence to support these actions.

(ii) Therefore, the railway authority must remember that it should work in coordination with the Revenue Department, the Department of Land Records, and the farmers must be taken into confidence by providing them the appropriate compensation.

5. Other demands include:

I. Indapur Taluka 

(i) Urgent requirement of an overbridge (flyover) at the railway crossing located on the Bhigwan?Rajejan road.

(ii) Scheduled halt of all express trains at Bhigwan.

m . Baramati Taluka

(i) Introduction of high speed rail services on the Baramati?Daund?Pune and Baramati?Mumbai routes.

(ii) At Undawadi K.P. (Jaradwadi) on the Daund?Baramati railway line, a railway crossing gate previously existed at kilometer marker 294/0. However, this gate was closed as part of a broader policy decision to eliminate such level crossings across the railway network. However, as a result, nearly 150 farmers whose approximately 500 acres of agricultural land lie on the opposite side of the railway line are facing serious difficulties in accessing their fields. They are now forced to take a detour of nearly 8 kilometers to reach their farmland. This situation has also led to a sharp increase in transportation costs, as drivers of tractors and other agricultural vehicles are charging significantly higher fares due to the longer travel distance. Hence, affected farmers are collectively demanding that an underpass (culvert/passage) be constructed at kilometer marker 294/0 on the Daund?Baramati railway line, precisely at the location where the railway crossing gate previously existed. This will facilitate safe and convenient access for commuting.

(iii) The Goods Shed at Baramati frequently leads to traffic congestion at the railway station. Therefore, the Goods Shed should be relocated to an area situated outside the city limits.

DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE (SHIRUR): The Union Railway Budget 2026-27, while masquerading under the grand narrative of ₹2.93 lakh crore record capital expenditure, is, in reality, a document of profound fiscal fragility and strategic neglect. Behind the "Viksit Bharat" branding lies a national transporter that is barely solvent, operating on a razor-thin Operating Ratio of 98.4%. This is not a budget of surplus; it is a budget of survival, where 90% of revenue is consumed by committed liabilities like salaries, pensions, and escalating lease payments to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC).

The Government presents a figure of ₹2.93 lakh crore as a "record allocation" for Railways. But looking closer, the "Viksit" dream looks more like a fiscal nightmare. We are a behemoth that consumes almost everything it earns. Where is the internal resource mobilization? We are running the world's fourth-largest rail network on borrowed oxygen.

I would like to bring attention of the Government to an important issue that concerns not only a railway project but also the fundamental principles of transparency, accountability, and respect for Parliament. The matter relates to the Pune?Nashik Semi-High-Speed Railway Project, a long-pending project that holds immense importance for the people of Western Maharashtra.

On 3rd December 2025, in response to a Starred Question in Lok Sabha, the Hon?ble Minister stated that the original Narayangaon alignment was abandoned solely due to technical objections regarding electromagnetic interference with the GMRT observatory.

We take pride in GMRT?s scientific legacy, but an RTI reply dated 14 January 2026 reveals a far more complex reality. When asked for technical proof of incompatibility, the NCRA claimed reports were ?too detailed to share.? This is unacceptable for a project of such public importance. The RTI further reveals that as early as November 2021, the NCRA did not demand a total shift. Instead, they proposed five engineering solutions including underground tunneling, electromagnetic shielding, and slight rerouting citing successful international models in Europe and the US. They even suggested a Joint Working Group to harmonize science with connectivity. इसका अर्थ क्या है? It means the alignment change was an administrative choice, not a technical necessity. अब एक सीधा सवाल है, अगर इतने सारे तकनीकी विकल्प उपलब्ध थे, तो क्या उन विकल्पों का गंभीरता से परीक्षण किया गया? I urge the Government to:

1. Place the full feasibility studies of the NCRA?s suggested mitigation measures before this House.

2. Explain why a Joint Technical Committee was bypassed in favor of a route that triples travel time.

Also, the originally proposed alignment was not merely a line on a map. It was expected to bring development and connectivity to the Junnar and Ambegaon talukas, regions that have long remained outside major industrial corridors. For the farmers, small industries, and young people of these regions, this railway project represents economic opportunity, agricultural logistics, employment, and regional balance.

Therefore, if the alignment is altered, the decision must be supported by clear and transparent technical evidence. The objective of this original project was to connect the two metropolitan cities of Pune and Nashik within 2 hours, and the distance via the original alignment was 235 km. In the Shirdi route alignment suggested by the Railway Minister, this same distance exceeds approximately 350 km, resulting in a travel time of around 7-8 hours.

I would now like to add another matter of profound strategic and social consequence, a project that sits at the very intersection of our industrial ambitions and our commitment to the soil. I speak of the Uruli-Alandi-Talegaon Railway corridor, a transformative artery destined to pulse life into the High-Density Network of our great nation.

The vision before us is grand. We are architecting a solution to decongest the overburdened heart of Pune and forge a seamless logistical link between the western industrial citadels of Chakan and Talegaon and the burgeoning logistics frontiers of the east at Uruli Kanchan. This project is the missing link that will unify the Mumbai-Pune-Daund-Hyderabad section.

However, progress that ignores the heartbeat of the village square is but a hollow victory. We must acknowledge the ground reality: the current proposed alignment traverses densely inhabited agrarian belts in Khed Taluka. The Talegaon-Alandi-Uruli railway alignment has been opposed by 12 villages in Khed taluka, and resolutions have been passed in the Gram Sabhas. Villages in Maval and Haveli talukas have also strongly opposed it.

To this end, a meticulously considered new alignment has been proposed to the Railway Board. This route spans from Kanhe to Navlakh Umbre, weaving through Koregaon Khurd (Chakan Phase 5), Rohkal, Waki Budruk, Kalus, Koyali, Aapti Phulgaon, Bakori, Gavdevwadi, and Koregaon Mul, before rejoining the mainline at Uruli Kanchan. By adopting this path, we do not just lay steel; we build consensus. This alignment allows for the integration of rail infrastructure with the planned Ring Road corridor. This multi-modal approach will optimize land utilization and minimize the fragmentation of precious farmland.

I call upon this Government to institutionalize a regular dialogue with our Gram Panchayats and elected officials. Let us mandate a rigorous Social Impact Assessment before the finalization of any Detailed Project Report.

I would also like to advocate for a paradigm shift: the move toward Road-Rail Co-location. The weight of international expertise from the World Bank to the OECD is unanimous. They speak of ?Multimodal Spines.? Currently, when land is acquired for an access-controlled highway, it is typically done to the extent of 110 meters. In a nation where landholdings are diminishing, we cannot afford fragmented acquisition. I propose that whenever large-scale land acquisition takes place for a highway project, the planning and reservation for a parallel railway track must be integrated at the very outset.

In this context, I wish to highlight two specific projects:

1. Extension of the Kalyan?Murbad?Ahmednagar line: This must be extended via Malshej Ghat to Ahmednagar to act as a vital lifeline for the Marathwada region.

2. Alternative Mumbai-Pune Corridor: I have proposed the route Uran?Panvel?Neral?Vandre?Pite?Shiroli?Pabal?Malthan?Shirur. This 133 km corridor is explicitly positioned as an alternative to the overburdened Mumbai?Pune Expressway. Between Neral and Vandre lies a challenging 20 km cliff-type ghat section. This is exactly where road-rail co-location is most compelling. If we protect the geometry for an adjacent track now, we create a future rail-capable Sahyadri crossing.

Furthermore, I present a vision for the proposed Private Railway Corridor linking JNPT to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. JNPT handles 65% of India?s container traffic, yet connectivity to Chakan, Talegaon, and Ranjangaon remains tethered to road transport. We envision a 420-kilometer fully private rail corridor, operated under a BOOT model for 60 years. This would reduce logistics costs by 30-40% and acts as a physical manifestation of the PM Gati Shakti vision.

Now, I consider it my moral responsibility to bring forth a distressing incident at Badlapur Railway Station. A woman passenger on Platform No. 3 was heartlessly denied access to a paid toilet facility because she did not possess the exact change. Under Minimum Essential Amenities norms, toilets are a fundamental right, not a luxury. I demand a factual inquiry into this incident and a mandate for flexible payment options, including UPI, across all stations.

The Budget reveals a dangerous trend. In 2024-25, 8.4% of our capex went to IRFC repayments. Today, it has ballooned to 13.5%. By 2028, we will be paying more to banks than we spend on laying new tracks. Is this a Budget for "Speed" or a Budget for "Debt"?

Furthermore, safety cannot be a PR exercise. The Ministry has missed its second consecutive deadline for Kavach installation. We have only covered 1,300 route km out of 68,000 km. While we talk of Vande Bharat, the common man in general coaches travels in "atrocious conditions" without basic protection.

Maharashtra is an economic powerhouse, yet there is a troubling gap between announcements and tangible outcomes. Projects worth ₹90,000 crore have been sanctioned, but completion remains elusive. The time has come for railway policy to move from projections to performance.

Infrastructure is about trust. When projects are delayed or altered without transparency, public confidence erodes. The people of Maharashtra seek fairness, clarity, and accountability.

If technical concerns exist, address them with science. If costs escalate, tell this House why. Development and scientific progress are not opposing forces. Our responsibility is to ensure both advance together.

As we say in Marathi, ?जनतेचा विश्वास हाच लोकशाहीची खरी ताकद आहे? (The trust of the people is the true strength of democracy). Let us ensure that infrastructure projects in Maharashtra are guided by evidence and the genuine aspirations of the people.

श्रीमती मालविका देवी (कालाहाण्डी) : नमस्कार, माननीय सभापति महोदया । मैं रेल मंत्रालय की अनुदानों की अनुपूरक माँगों के समर्थन में इस सदन में अपनी बात रखने के लिए खड़ी हुई हूँ । यह वही रेल मंत्रालय है, जहाँ हमने देखा है कि विपक्ष भी अपना पक्ष भूलकर सत्ता दल के साथ एक ही सुर में बोलने लगता है । इसके लिए मैं प्रधान मंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी और रेल मंत्री श्री अश्‍विनी वैष्णव जी का आभार व्यक्त करती हूँ, जिन्होंने देश के विकास का नेतृत्व करते हुए रेलवे को एक नई दिशा दी है । 

मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र कालाहाण्डी में रेलवे के विकास की एक नई परिभाषा लिखी गई है । इसके लिए मैं फिर क्षेत्र के लोगों की तरफ से प्रधान मंत्री जी और रेल मंत्री जी को धन्यवाद देती हूँ कि उन्होंने मेरी माँगों का ध्यान रखकर उन्हें मंजूरी दी है । चाहे वह जूनागढ़-नबरंगपुर रेलवे लाइन का विस्तार हो, नुआपाड़ा-बरगढ़ रेलवे लाइन का विस्तार हो, केसिंगा और खरियार रोड पर दो वंदे भारत स्टेशन हों, केसिंगा, भवानीपटना और खरियार रोड पर तीन अमृत भारत स्टेशन हों, लांजीगढ़ में एक नई रेलवे लाइन हो, इस्पात ट्रेन का विस्तार कांटाबांजी से जूनागढ़, केसिंगा, भवानीपटना, लांजीगढ़ तक हो, धनबाद-अल्लेप्पी एक्सप्रेस का नारला में ठहराव हो, एक अमृत भारत एक्सप्रेस का केसिंगा और खरियार रोड पर ठहराव हो । भवानीपटना के लिए दूसरे प्लेटफॉर्म की मंजूरी मिल गई है । जूनागढ़ रोड स्टेशन पर माल गोदाम के उन्नयन का काम चल रहा है, इसके लिए बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद ।

भारत के केंद्रीय बजट 2026-27 में भारतीय रेलवे के लिए रिकॉर्ड 2.93 लाख करोड़ रुपये आवंटित किए गए हैं, जो अब तक का सबसे बड़ा आवंटन है । 2.81 लाख करोड़ रुपये की प्रत्यक्ष फंडिंग का समर्थन हुआ है । राजस्व में नौ प्रतिशत की वृद्धि का अनुमान है, 87,300 करोड़ रुपये हो जाएगा ।

हाई-स्पीड कॉरिडोर, सात नए कॉरिडोर्स को ग्रोथ कनेक्टर के तौर पर घोषित किया गया है । इनका मकसद पर्यावरण के अनुकूल यात्री यात्रा को बढ़ावा देना है । एक ईस्ट वेस्ट फ्रेट कॉरिडोर डांकुनी से सूरत तक लॉजिस्टिक्स को बेहतर करने के लिए बनाया गया है । 

जिन क्षेत्रों पर खास ध्यान दिया जा रहा है, उनमें ट्रैक का दोहरीकरण, पूरी तरह से विद्युतीकरण, कवच सुरक्षा प्रणाली का विस्तार और वंदे भारत स्लीपर ट्रेन की शुरुआत शामिल हैं । ईस्ट-वेस्ट डेडिकेटेड फ्रेट कॉरिडोर 2,000 किलोमीटर से ज्यादा लंबा है, ओडिशा में रेलवे के बुनियादी ढाँचे में महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव देखने को मिले हैं । 

वर्ष 2009 से वर्ष 2014 की अवधि के मुकाबले इसका औसत वार्षिक बजट 13 गुना बढ़ा दिया गया है । 10,928 करोड़ रुपये का आवंटन मिला है, यह धनराशि 90,659 करोड़ रुपये की परियोजनाओं को समर्थन देती है, जिनमें पटरियों का विस्तार और विद्युतीकरण शामिल है । यह पिछली सरकारों के समय के औसत आवंटन से 13 गुना अधिक है ।

हमारे राज्य को पूर्व पश्चिम सम्पर्क मालगाड़ी कॉरिडोर से सीधा लाभ मिला है, जो ओडिशा से होकर गुजरात, छत्तीसगढ़, मध्य प्रदेश और महाराष्ट्र से जुड़ता है । अमृत स्टेशन योजना के तहत 59 स्टेशनों का पुनर्विकास 2,500 करोड़ रुपये की लागत से किया जा रहा है । छः वंदे भारत और छः अमृत भारत ट्रेन्स संचालित हो रही हैं । पिछले 11 वर्षो में 2,200 किलोमीटर नई रेल पटरियाँ बिछाई गई हैं । 

मैं अंत में कालाहाण्डी के लिए कुछ माँगे रखना चाहूँगी । भवानी पटना से कांटाबाजी की ROB, केसिंगा से भुवनेश्वर के लिए सीधी ट्रेन, नारला रोड रेलवे स्टेशन पर लोकोमोटिव, नारला रखरखाव/मरम्मत कारखाना, जो कि बहुत पुरानी माँग है, अश्‍विनी जी जानते हैं । नारला रोड रेलवे स्टेशन पर ट्रेन सेवा की बहाली, समता एक्सप्रेस और तिरुपति एक्सप्रेस का ठहराव हो ।

सभापति महोदया जी, मेरी कुछ मांगें हैं - जूनागढ़-नबरंगपुर के लिए धर्मगढ़ में नया रेलवे स्‍टेशन; रुपरा रोड स्‍टेशन पर एक्‍सप्रेस एक्‍सप्रेस ट्रेन्‍स जैसे समता, तिरुपति और अहमदाबाद पुरी एक्‍सप्रेस, सम्‍बलपुर-नांदेड़ एक्‍सप्रेस के ठहराव की बहाली । नारला रोड रेलवे स्‍टेशन पर रेलवे ओवर‍ब्रिज; भुवनेश्‍वर से रायगढ़, कोरापुट के लिए टिटलागढ़ होते हुए सीधी ट्रेन की शुरूआत । नुआपाड़ा, नारला रोड पर समता एक्‍सप्रेस ट्रेन का ठहराव । किसानों की आवाजाही को सुगम बनाने के लिए एक भूमिगत रेलवे ओवरब्रिज का निर्माण जो कुत्रुखामार रेलवे स्‍टेशन पर हो सकता है । कुत्रुखामार रेलवे स्‍टेशन की ओर 40 किलोमीटर पर रेलवे लाइन पार करने के लिए अस्‍थायी मार्ग ट्रेसपासिंग की अनुमति होनी चाहिए । जूनागढ़ रोड, ओडिशा, बैंगलुरू सिटी रेलवे स्‍टेशन्‍स या यशवंतपुर, कर्नाटक राज्‍य के लिए ट्रेन; जनजातीय गौरव कोरिडोर याेजना के तहत नुआपाड़ा-बोलंगीर, ओडिशा से भद्राचलम तेलंगाना तक रेलवे लाइन का विस्‍तार; जूनागढ़ रोड से भुवनेश्‍वर जाने वाली ट्रेन का देयपुर में ठहराव; खारियार के रास्‍ते कांटाबांजी और धर्मगढ़ के बीच रेलवे लाइन के लिए संशोधित अनुमान, जिसे कांटाबांजी से जयपुर मार्ग के स्थान पर प्रस्‍ताव किया जाना चाहिए ।

केंद्रीय जनजातीय गौरव कोरिडोर का विस्‍तार जिसमें भद्राचलम को शामिल किया जाए । खारियार, सीनापाली और कोमना के रास्‍ते धर्मगढ़ से नुआपाड़ा तक कांटाबांजी तथा पटनागढ़ के रास्ते खारियार से बोलंगीर की परियाोजना भारत के तीन राज्‍यों छत्‍तीसगढ़, ओडिशा और आंध्र प्रदेश को जोड़ेगी । तांजीगढ़ -जूनागढ़ रेलवे लाइन का दोहरीकरण । जूनागढ़ रोड-संभलपुर, जूनागढ़ रोड-रायपुर, भवानीपटना और विशाखापट्नम के लिए पैसेंजर ट्रेन दी जाए ।
